page: Amazon Web Services m7g.2xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton3 processor family. Built on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture operating at 2.6 GHz, the instance delivers 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating virtualized hyperthreading contention. Compute cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware-accelerated cryptographic routines are supported via dedicated AES instructions, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture.

The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes no integrated local NVMe storage, relying entirely on remote elastic block storage volumes over the Nitro fabric. Dedicated network bandwidth provides a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps. Acceleration hardware is not included, with a zero GPU count.

Benchmark assessments display balanced performance across typical enterprise workloads. In multi-threaded computational benchmarks, the instance registered 12,247.03 on stress-ng and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 8,124.0, complemented by an 11,775.0 score in Clang compilation. In-memory data throughput is an architectural strength, indicated by a strong top-quartile PassMark memory score of 2,868.55 and memory read bandwidth peaking at 773.36 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks. Static web serving throughput reached 15.41 GB/sec, alongside 13.12 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks.

Tradeoffs emerge in specialized vector processing, legacy integer tests, and large-scale AI models. Without x86 AVX extensions, the PassMark CPU suite rated lower at 6,070.64, driven by a weak encryption subscore of 1,115.06. Additionally, medium 7B model LLM prompt processing fell into the bottom decile at 14.12 tokens per second. Consequently, m7g.2xlarge offers qualitative efficiency when running arm64-native distributed microservices, Redis caching layers, web frontends, and build pipelines rather than raw cryptographic pipelines or local storage databases.
description: Amazon Web Services m7g.2xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose server powered by 8 dedicated AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 cores clocked at 2.6 GHz, coupled with 32.0 GB of system RAM at a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it includes 4 Gbps baseline network throughput, no bundled local SSD storage, and no hardware GPU accelerators. The instance achieves competitive throughput in continuous integration and in-memory caching workloads, verified by an 11,775.0 Clang compilation score and a top-quartile PassMark memory mark of 2,868.55. However, the absence of x86-specific vector extensions leads to lower results in selected synthetic CPU tests, and LLM prompt processing remains limited. The m7g.2xlarge is cost-efficient for arm64-compiled web services, container hosts, CI/CD runners, and distributed key-value stores.
